nodes.label: Permanent Data Source Hierarchy
nodes.rationale: Local SQLite is the one and only source used to build ML datasets; Firestore, Google Sheets, REST APIs, Cloud Functions and cached cloud responses are forbidden inputs and Google Sheets is an OUTPUT destination only.

nodes.label: getBusinessDate()
nodes.rationale: There is no single shared date utility; at least seven competing implementations exist (device-local, '-1 hour', raw UTC, fixed Dhaka), which is the root cause of the documented inconsistencies.

nodes.label: Midnight (12:00 AM) Business-Day Rollover
nodes.rationale: Core POS transactions roll over strictly at local midnight with no 4 AM grace period; only deliveries, dashboard month pickers, and telemetry have offsets, so the restaurant day for orders/payments/expenses is the calendar day.

nodes.label: ADMIN-Exempt Version Gating Rule
nodes.rationale: ADMIN build profile bypasses startup version gating so an administrator is never locked out of the management console by a faulty update push.

nodes.label: Firebase-Only Version Control
nodes.rationale: The version policy lives in the Firestore app_config/global document and blocks the whole app behind AppUpdateRequiredScreen; ADMIN is always exempt so an admin can never be locked out of their own terminal.

nodes.label: Rolling 31-day retention policy (13 rolling tables)
nodes.rationale: The Supabase free-tier constraint is egress (5 GB/mo) and device battery/data, not request count, so pruning >31-day rows from the 13 rolling tables bounds payload size while Firebase and local SQLite keep full history.

nodes.label: daily_submit deterministic priority tie-breaker (priority → submitted_at → device_id)
nodes.norm_label: daily_submit deterministic priority tie-breaker (priority → submitted_at → device_id)

nodes.label: Deferred conflict races (expenses stable-ID, supplier_payment_ledger INSERT-OR-REPLACE, supplier_due running balance)
nodes.norm_label: deferred conflict races (expenses stable-id, supplier_payment_ledger insert-or-replace, supplier_due running balance)

nodes.label: EXPO_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_SYNC_ENABLED Kill Switch
nodes.rationale: Provides an instant, no-code-revert path back to Firebase-only behavior, which is what makes the additive migration safely rollbackable per phase.

nodes.label: ALLOW_AUTO_FIREBASE_READ = false policy + FIREBASE_FIRST_SYNC_DAYS = 31
nodes.rationale: 2k+ automatic Firestore reads/day with no manual pull traced to a failure-triggered whole-group Firebase fallback (low-freq group = 17 collections), the sticky failed-writes gate, and a cursor-less table being read as the ENTIRE collection; the policy trades 'app reads nothing while Supabase is unhealthy' for near-zero automatic Firebase reads.

nodes.label: Device Control stays 100% Supabase-only (permanent owner decision)
nodes.norm_label: device control stays 100% supabase-only (permanent owner decision)
nodes.rationale: The app owner decided Device Control stays 100% Supabase-only by design; no Firebase fallback will be built, the earlier plan is withdrawn and partial work reverted, and the accepted cost is that non-ADMIN devices with allow_offline=0 cannot pass the gate while Supabase is unreachable.

nodes.label: Dual-write (parallel independent Firebase + Supabase queues)
nodes.rationale: Writes go to Firebase sync_queue and Supabase sync_queue_supabase as parallel independent queues with per-backend retry, delegated via lazy require + nested try/catch so a Supabase failure can never affect Firebase.

nodes.label: getRestoreMode() fresh-install restore scope (MANAGER today / ADMIN-OWNER 31d / unresolved today)
nodes.norm_label: getrestoremode() fresh-install restore scope (manager today / admin-owner 31d / unresolved today)
nodes.rationale: A Manager fresh install pulled ~18-19k rows because build profiles that did not set EXPO_PUBLIC_APP_PROFILE silently received the ADMIN 31-day scope; the fix makes an unresolved profile today-only (fail-conservative).

nodes.label: Push-on-write to both clouds (syncRecordImmediately parallel pushes)
nodes.norm_label: push-on-write to both clouds (syncrecordimmediately parallel pushes)

nodes.label: Read-routing gate (Firebase reads only on failure / >31-day data)
nodes.norm_label: read-routing gate (firebase reads only on failure / >31-day data)
nodes.rationale: Owner target: normal use = Supabase reads only; Firebase read ONLY when Supabase fails or when data is older than 31 days — because Firebase quota/egress (not request count) is the real constraint, while writes stay dual.

nodes.label: Firebase + Supabase Dual-DB Migration
nodes.rationale: Supabase is pure-additive: the Firebase path stays byte-for-byte untouched, every Supabase error is swallowed, and a kill switch restores Firebase-only behavior instantly.

nodes.label: Realtime change-signal + adaptive slow safety poll
nodes.norm_label: realtime change-signal + adaptive slow safety poll

nodes.label: Supabase-first login cloud check (Firebase 429 no longer blocks login)
nodes.norm_label: supabase-first login cloud check (firebase 429 no longer blocks login)

nodes.label: Automatic Receipt Printing Policy
nodes.rationale: Silent auto-print surprised operators, printed paid receipts before customers asked, and wasted thermal paper; printing is now guarded by auto_print_enabled (default off) with manual print preserved.

nodes.label: Pre-Phase-2 backfill gap (FK violation on owner_salary_ledger)
nodes.norm_label: pre-phase-2 backfill gap (fk violation on owner_salary_ledger)

nodes.label: AdminAnalyticsScreen (PRIMARY MIXED case)
nodes.rationale: It queries daily_submit across ALL time with no date bound and lets the user compare any two arbitrary periods; it is the only screen that genuinely spans beyond the 31-day window, which forces daily_submit/daily_summary to retain full lifetime history.

nodes.label: DailyItemSalesReport Cloud Download
nodes.rationale: Custom calendar picks trigger fetchHistoricalDateData for a single day only (limit 7 cloud downloads/day), so no UI path ever produces a merged recent+historical multi-date result.

nodes.label: Mixed Date-Range View Classification (A/B/C)
nodes.rationale: Screens are classified as recent-only, historical-only, or genuinely mixed so that only the mixed case needs cross-time-range read capability after migration.

nodes.label: 31-Day Local Data Window
nodes.rationale: Transaction tables are restored only for the last 31 days while master/reference tables are always fully synced; this is the boundary that defines which screens can read locally.

nodes.label: Date-First Transactional Tables
nodes.rationale: Tables carrying an explicit YYYY-MM-DD column are trivially retention-filterable, unlike tables that must derive the business day from a UTC timestamp.

nodes.label: 31-Day Retention Cutoff Filter Map
nodes.rationale: Per-table WHERE clauses were mapped so a pg_cron job can delete >31-day rows; daily_submit and daily_summary are explicitly exempt because analytics needs full history.

nodes.label: daily_submit/daily_summary Firebase-Only Read Decision
nodes.rationale: Dual-written to Supabase but never read back, which guarantees AdminAnalyticsScreen keeps full lifetime history regardless of Supabase retention.

nodes.label: Zero Regression Policy
nodes.rationale: Owner App, Manager App and POS billing workflows stay 100% untouched; submitDailySheet, Ijara and deposit calculations remain independent and unmodified.

nodes.label: Android Signing Conflict (INSTALL_FAILED_UPDATE_INCOMPATIBLE -7)
nodes.rationale: Uninstalling bypasses the signature conflict but immediately wipes un-synced offline SQLite transactions, printer pairings and cached auth; the only correct fix is to rebuild the APK with the exact original signing key.

nodes.label: Exponential Backoff Retry (30s → 10min)
nodes.rationale: There is deliberately no circuit breaker; failed items are retried forever with min(10min, 2^retryCount × 30s) so a transient outage always self-heals.

nodes.label: Force Logout Command
nodes.rationale: Delivered by Realtime (<300ms) with a 60-second safety poll; the old 1-second poll was removed because it cost ~3,600 REST GETs/hr/device for no added safety.

nodes.label: safeSupabaseCall
nodes.rationale: Swallows every Supabase error and returns a fallback value so POS operations are structurally incapable of being blocked by Supabase failures.

nodes.label: app_version_policy Table
nodes.rationale: Public SELECT is required because the version check runs before device approval; only UPDATE is admin-device gated.

nodes.label: Supabase-Only Device Control System
nodes.rationale: Device fleet management was fully decommissioned from Firestore (syncDeviceRegistry returns false, clearDeadQueueItems purges pending device_registry items) and moved to Supabase so device approval and revocation are isolated from POS data.

nodes.label: Supabase Realtime Presence
nodes.rationale: Presence is in-memory over WebSocket with zero DB writes (25s heartbeat, 45s stale threshold); last_seen_at is persisted only every 2 minutes to avoid write overhead.

nodes.label: R6 — Realtime vs RLS Risk
nodes.rationale: X-Device-Id is a PostgREST header and cannot authenticate Realtime postgres_changes, so strict RLS may block POS Realtime; mitigation is limiting realtime to restaurant_tables or falling back to 8s polling.

nodes.label: Device-Approval-Gated Row Level Security
nodes.rationale: Every Supabase request carries X-Device-Id and a SECURITY DEFINER function validates device state before allowing POS reads/writes, so an unapproved device fails closed on business data.

nodes.label: PENDING Device RLS Exceptions
nodes.rationale: A PENDING device must still INSERT its own devices row, write telemetry, and SELECT app_version_policy — otherwise the version check that runs before approval would trap it in an error loop.

nodes.label: Expenses Stable-ID Overwrite Race
nodes.rationale: id = exp_{date}_{category} plus INSERT OR REPLACE means two devices editing the same category on the same day silently last-write-win; no conflict detection exists.

nodes.label: Supplier Due Running-Balance Lost Update
nodes.rationale: saveSupplierDue does read-modify-write on a shared mutable aggregate with no compare-and-swap; recommended fix is an append-only ledger with server-side SUM().

nodes.label: Supplier Payment Ledger 48h Lock
nodes.rationale: Entry age >48h blocks only non-Admins; this is post-edit protection, not a write-conflict guard, and submitDailySheet auto-fill can overwrite manual entries.

nodes.label: activity_logs UTC business_date Leak
nodes.rationale: now.toISOString().split('T')[0] yields the UTC date, so actions between 00:00 and 05:59 BST are logged to yesterday; this must be fixed before the retention cutoff can trust business_date.

nodes.label: Phase 4 — Correctness & Conflict Fixes
nodes.rationale: Deliberately sequenced BEFORE retention because the retention cutoff's correctness depends on the activity_logs business_date being fixed.

nodes.label: 5-Second Push Daemon (processSyncQueue)
nodes.rationale: Offline-first design: every write lands in SQLite first and a background queue pushes to Firestore asynchronously, so POS operation never blocks on network.

nodes.label: Multi-Device Write Conflicts
nodes.rationale: Firestore has no row-level locking, so the sync model is optimistic last-write-wins on updated_at; the 5-second queue daemon makes a 5-second conflict window realistic across the three app profiles.

nodes.label: daily_submit Priority System
nodes.rationale: Owner(100) > Admin(50) > Manager(10) priority means a lower-privilege submission can never overwrite a higher-privilege EOD sheet; same-role multi-device ties are still unresolved (last PATCH wins).

nodes.label: Timestamp-Only Transactional Tables
nodes.rationale: orders/order_items/payments/expenses/deliveries/due_payments have no business_date column; their day is evaluated dynamically via date(created_at,'localtime'), which makes retention cutoffs fragile.

nodes.label: Device-Local Timezone Handling (no Asia/Dhaka enforcement)
nodes.rationale: The app assumes the POS tablet is set to BST; relying on SQLite 'localtime' and JS local getters means a misconfigured device silently shifts every business date, and no Intl timeZone usage exists in the transaction path.

nodes.label: 27/27 device-gated POS tables (devices, device_app_usage, app_version_policy excluded)
nodes.norm_label: 27/27 device-gated pos tables (devices, device_app_usage, app_version_policy excluded)

nodes.label: Permissive anon access (Phase 1) policy
nodes.rationale: Postgres ORs permissive policies, so every Phase 7 gate block must DROP the Phase 1 permissive policy first, otherwise device gating would be a silent no-op.

nodes.label: APP_PROFILES (ADMIN/OWNER/MANAGER)
nodes.rationale: One codebase produces three APKs by compile-time EXPO_PUBLIC_APP_PROFILE; the profile constant cannot change at runtime, which guarantees a Manager APK can never behave as Admin.

nodes.label: Firebase Anonymous Authentication
nodes.rationale: Anonymous auth is purely a machine-to-Firestore transport credential; app-level user login stays PIN-based in SQLite so Firebase identity never entangles with business identity.

nodes.label: Firestore REST API v1
nodes.rationale: No Firebase JS SDK is used; every Firestore call is a raw fetch() against the REST API v1, which keeps the app free of the firebase npm package and usable from Expo.

nodes.label: resyncSameDayFromCloud
nodes.rationale: Rate-limited to 2 runs per business day to bound cost while still allowing recovery from bad same-day state.

nodes.label: restaurant_tables Last-Write-Wins
nodes.rationale: No lock or priority field exists on restaurant_tables, so the 15-second pull window is the key vulnerability when two devices tap the same FREE table.

nodes.label: Phase 3 — Read Routing (Supabase-Primary Pull)
nodes.rationale: Read routing is implemented in the sync layer so screens keep reading SQLite unchanged (zero screen changes); Firebase timers stay running as fallback in the same tick.

nodes.label: Delta Pull via updated_at Cursor
nodes.rationale: last_sync_time_{table} cursors plus a 60-second overlap guard avoid full-collection reads; the previous whole-collection fetch caused multi-thousand-document read bursts.

nodes.label: restoreDatabaseFromCloud Full-Restore Flow
nodes.rationale: Splits tables into alwaysFull, recentOnly (31 days) and skipRestoreMarkers so a fresh install gets master data plus a bounded transactional window without a read storm.

nodes.label: Pull Polling Intervals (5s/15s/30s/90s/180s)
nodes.rationale: Interval tiers are matched to data freshness needs: tables 15s, orders/payments 30s, deletions 90s, master data 180s, push 5s.

nodes.label: Schema Guardian (PRAGMA table_info)
nodes.rationale: Reads the local table columns at pull time and inserts only columns that exist locally, so an older app build never crashes on a newer cloud schema.

nodes.label: R1 — Bootstrap Gap for Fresh-Install Restore
nodes.norm_label: r1 — bootstrap gap for fresh-install restore
nodes.rationale: Existing deployments have no Supabase POS history until dual-write accumulates, so a fresh install restoring from Supabase would see an empty 31-day window (apparent data loss); mitigation is hybrid restore or a one-time Firebase→Supabase backfill.
